items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: Of course, I left Earl and I went to New York to join Jimmy Lunceford

ctx.x: He was a terrific showman. And as most people found out when he went with Duke, he really got the proper exposure with Duke. And Duke admired him. Duke told us that Ray Nance never played a wrong note. You know, I thought that was a beautiful statement that he made about him.

Of course, I left Earl and I went to New York to join Jimmy Lunceford, and this is when I really began to get a little name among the public because Jimmy was very popular with recordings in those days. And we did a lot of -- had a chance to play a lot of solos. I was very fortunate because he didn't have a trombone player prior to the time I came in there that did a lot of solo work. So, I got an opportunity to play a lot of solos. He had two good trombone players but they weren't really soloists, you know. They…
Had you been soloing a lot with Earl Hines?
